name: St. Croix River — Upper
gaugeName: ST. CROIX RIVER NEAR DANBURY, WI
blurb: The upper St. Croix in the St. Croix National Scenic Riverway between Wisconsin-side NPS and Wisconsin DNR-listed landings, with NPS river miles.

timing.note: A reviewed speed/flow calibration has not been established. Access and guide information remain available.

sections.putIn: Gordon Dam Park Landing (St. Croix NSR)
sections.takeOut: County Road T Landing (St. Croix NSR)
sections.notes: Markers identify agency-listed access; the map states whether a landing or an approximate facility area has been reviewed. Mileage follows the agency river-mile information cited in the research. Difficulty has not been independently rated for every section. Check current conditions, hazards and access with the managing agency before paddling.

notices.title: Portage information
notices.text: St. Croix Falls / Taylors Falls hydroelectric dam: NPS river map: "There is a 3.1 mile portage around the dam … through Taylors Falls, Minnesota." The upper and lower St. Croix reaches are separate catalog rivers; no section crosses the dam.
notices.sourceName: NPS St. Croix NSR — river map 7

notices.title: River hazard
notices.text: NPS St. Croix paddling guide: "Approximately 300 yards of boulders, plus Class 1 and II rapids come up suddenly before the Scott Bridge (S153.4). It is best to stay to the left when paddling these rapids."
notices.sourceName: NPS St. Croix NSR — Paddling Guide to the St. Croix River, Gordon Dam to Highway 70 (distance chart)

notices.title: Portage information
notices.text: NPS St. Croix paddling guide: "You can sometimes run the chute of … Coppermine Dam (S148.8), but make sure you scout it first (the chute second from the right is usually best) or use the portage on the right."
notices.sourceName: NPS St. Croix NSR — Paddling Guide to the St. Croix River, Gordon Dam to Highway 70 (distance chart)

notices.title: Use the below-dam canoe launch
notices.text: Start at the designated canoe launch below Gordon Dam, shown in the county park guide. The separate ramp on the flowage is upstream of the dam and is not the start for this trip. County T remains an approximate access-area marker.
notices.sourceName: Douglas County — Gordon Dam County Park guide

notices.title: River hazard
notices.text: NPS St. Croix paddling guide: "Calm water ends once you reach Big Fish Trap Rapids (S140.0). These winding Class I and II … rapids are considered the most challenging on the Riverway and no portage exists."
notices.sourceName: NPS St. Croix NSR — Paddling Guide to the St. Croix River, Gordon Dam to Highway 70 (distance chart)

notices.title: River hazard
notices.text: NPS St. Croix paddling guide (CCC Bridge Landing, S138.9): "there is a smaller set of Class I rapids called Little Fish Trap Rapids. Make a sharp left turn under the bridge to reach the landing."
notices.sourceName: NPS St. Croix NSR — Paddling Guide to the St. Croix River, Gordon Dam to Highway 70 (distance chart)
